name: Citrus-Marinated Salmon Bowl
description: Salmon marinated in orange and soy, seared quick and served over brown rice with avocado, cucumber, and pickled ginger.
why: Salmon's omega-3s and a fiber-forward brown rice base make this steady and satisfying without asking you to give up flavor.
mods: Ask for the marinade on the side to control saltiness.
Swap in shredded cabbage for extra crunch and fiber.
watch: The soy marinade carries more sodium than it looks like it would.

name: Miso-Glazed Tofu Bowl
description: Pan-seared tofu brushed with a sweet-savory miso glaze, over rice with edamame, carrots, and a scatter of sesame seeds.
why: A complete plant protein with zero cholesterol, plus a genuinely fiber-forward bowl if you want a break from meat.
mods: Add extra vegetables instead of more rice if you want more volume.
A squeeze of lime brightens it up, skip if reflux is flaring.

name: Teriyaki Chicken Rice Bowl
description: Grilled chicken thigh glazed with teriyaki, over rice with steamed broccoli and a sprinkle of sesame.
why: A reliable, familiar bowl. The teriyaki brings real flavor, so the rest of the plate can stay simple.
mods: Ask for the glaze on the side, most places pour it on heavy.
Brown rice or a half-rice-half-greens swap adds fiber.
watch: Teriyaki glaze is one of the sneakier sources of added sugar on a menu.

name: Spicy Tuna Poke Bowl
description: Cubed raw tuna tossed in spicy mayo, served over rice with avocado, cucumber, and seaweed salad.
why: Tuna is lean and dense with almost no saturated fat, the spicy mayo is what to watch, not the fish.
mods: Ask for sauce on the side and add it yourself, a little goes a long way.
Half rice, half greens keeps this lighter without losing the bowl feel.
watch: Spicy mayo is a rich sauce, easy to overpour without noticing.

name: Sesame Beef Bibimbap
description: Thin-sliced beef with sesame oil, over rice with sautéed spinach, carrots, bean sprouts, and a fried egg on top.
why: A genuinely balanced plate: protein, a fried egg, and three different vegetables in one bowl.
mods: Choose a leaner cut and let the vegetables and sauce carry the richness.
Ask for gochujang on the side if you want to control the heat.
watch: Gochujang brings real heat and sodium both, a little covers the whole bowl.

name: Furikake Salmon Rice Bowl
description: Flaked salmon over warm rice with a generous dusting of furikake, avocado, and a drizzle of sesame-soy.
why: Simple and quick. Sometimes low effort is exactly the right goal, and the salmon still does real work here.
mods: Add a fried or soft-boiled egg for extra staying power.
Cucumber or radish adds crunch without much effort.

name: Ginger Shrimp Fried Rice
description: Wok-tossed rice with shrimp, egg, peas, and a generous amount of fresh ginger and scallion.
why: A classic wok pairing if shellfish isn't a concern for you, and the ginger does a lot of flavor work without added fat.
mods: Ask for light oil, fried rice can go heavy fast.
Add extra vegetables (carrot, cabbage) for more volume and fiber.
watch: Restaurant fried rice often uses more oil and sodium than a home version would.

name: Phở Gà
description: Chicken pho: a clear, ginger-and-star-anise broth over rice noodles with shredded chicken, herbs, and lime.
why: A light, plant-forward broth base with real herbs and a lean protein. Easy on the stomach and genuinely restorative.
mods: Ask for less noodles, more broth and herbs if you want it lighter.
Skip the hoisin and sriracha table sauces if reflux is a concern today.
watch: The broth can carry more sodium than it tastes like, especially at restaurants.

name: Bún Chả
description: Grilled pork patties and pork belly over cool vermicelli noodles with herbs, pickled carrot and daikon, and a tangy nước chấm on the side.
why: The grilling keeps this leaner than it tastes, and the herbs and pickle add real freshness against the richness of the pork.
mods: Choose a leaner cut and let the herbs and nước chấm carry the flavor.
Ask for nước chấm on the side so you control how much goes in.
watch: Nước chấm is easy to underestimate: sugar and sodium both hide in there.

name: Gỏi Cuốn
description: Fresh spring rolls: shrimp and pork wrapped in rice paper with vermicelli, herbs, and lettuce, served with peanut sauce.
why: Nothing here is fried. It's about as light and vegetable-forward as a wrapped roll gets.
mods: Ask for peanut sauce on the side, it's the richest part of the dish by far.
Add extra herbs and lettuce for more volume per roll.
watch: Peanut sauce is thick with sugar and fat both, a little goes a long way per roll.

name: Cơm Tấm Sườn Nướng
description: Grilled pork chop over broken rice, with a fried egg, pickled vegetables, and a side of nước chấm.
why: A hearty, genuinely satisfying plate. The grilled pork and pickled vegetables balance each other well.
mods: Ask for a smaller portion of rice and more pickled vegetables.
Nước chấm on the side, same as always, so you're in control.
watch: This is one of the larger portions on the menu, boxing half before you start is worth it.

name: Bún Bò Huế
description: A spicier, lemongrass-forward beef and pork noodle soup from central Vietnam, with thick round noodles and herbs.
why: Bold and warming, with real depth from the lemongrass and chili oil. Worth knowing it runs spicier than phở.
mods: Ask for chili oil on the side if you want to dial down the heat.
Extra herbs and bean sprouts add freshness and volume.
watch: This runs spicier and richer than a typical phở, and the broth carries real sodium.

name: Canh Chua Cá
description: Sweet and sour fish soup with tamarind, pineapple, tomato, okra, and bean sprouts, served with rice on the side.
why: A genuinely vegetable-forward soup. The tamarind's sourness is bright rather than heavy, and the fish keeps it light.
mods: Ask for a milder tamarind balance if you're sensitive to sour and spicy together.
Extra bean sprouts and herbs stretch the bowl without adding rice.
watch: The tamarind and pineapple make this one of the more acidic dishes on this list.

name: Cá Kho Tộ
description: Fish braised in a clay pot with caramelized fish sauce, black pepper, and a little sugar, served over rice.
why: Deeply savory in a small amount, this dish is built to be eaten with a lot of rice and isn't trying to be a big portion of fish.
mods: A small portion goes a long way, let the rice and a side vegetable round out the plate.
Add a simple stir-fried green vegetable on the side for fiber.
watch: The caramelized sauce is concentrated in sodium and sugar, this is a flavor-in-small-doses dish.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Diced chicken stir-fried with peanuts, dried chilies, and scallion in a savory-sweet sauce.
why: Takes on sauce beautifully without adding cholesterol. The peanuts add texture and a little staying power.
mods: Ask for the sauce on the lighter side, it's easy to overpour.
Half rice, half steamed vegetables lightens the plate.
watch: Dried chilies and a rich sauce together make this one to notice if you're sensitive to spice.

name: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
description: A whole or filleted fish steamed simply with ginger, scallion, and a light soy drizzle.
why: Stays well ahead of anything deep-fried. About as gentle a preparation as this list has.
mods: Ask for the soy drizzle on the side, this dish is meant to taste like the fish.
A side of steamed greens rounds this out well.

name: Mapo Tofu
description: Soft tofu simmered in a spicy, numbing sauce with ground pork and scallion, served over rice.
why: A satisfying option as long as it isn't breaded and fried first, and the tofu keeps this lighter than it tastes.
mods: Ask for a milder spice level if the numbing heat is a lot for you today.
A side of steamed vegetables adds volume without adding sauce.
watch: This is genuinely spicy and a common one to notice if you're managing reflux.

name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-fry
description: Thin-sliced beef and broccoli tossed in a garlic-soy sauce, served over rice.
why: A familiar, easy protein-and-vegetable combination. Choosing a leaner cut keeps this genuinely balanced.
mods: Choose a leaner cut and let the sauce and broccoli carry the dish.
Extra broccoli in place of some rice adds fiber for free.

name: Egg Drop Soup
description: A light chicken broth thickened slightly and swirled with beaten egg, with scallion on top.
why: Creamy texture without any actual cream. A gentle, low-effort option when you want something warm and light.
mods: Add tofu or extra vegetables to make this more of a full meal.
watch: Restaurant broth can run higher in sodium than the light taste suggests.

name: Cold Sesame Noodles
description: Chilled wheat noodles tossed in a sesame-peanut sauce with cucumber and scallion.
why: Simple and quick, a good choice when you want something cool and don't need much active cooking.
mods: Add shredded chicken or tofu to round this into a full meal.
Extra cucumber and shredded carrot add crunch and volume.
watch: Sesame-peanut sauce is rich, a little dressing goes a long way here.

name: Grilled Chicken Cobb Salad
description: Grilled chicken over mixed greens with tomato, egg, avocado, and a light vinaigrette.
why: A reliable lean option that still feels like a real meal, not just a side salad.
mods: Skip the bacon and cheese if they're on the version you're ordering, they're the biggest swing on saturated fat.
Ask for dressing on the side.
watch: Cobb salads at restaurants often come loaded with bacon and cheese by default, worth asking what's included.

name: Salmon and Avocado Salad
description: Flaked salmon over greens with avocado, cucumber, and a citrus vinaigrette.
why: Omega-3s that work directly in your favor, paired with a genuinely fiber-forward plate.
mods: Add a scoop of quinoa or chickpeas if you want more staying power.

name: Chickpea and Kale Salad
description: Massaged kale with roasted chickpeas, feta, and a lemon-olive oil dressing.
why: Plant protein and fiber in the same scoop. A genuinely filling salad, not just leaves.
mods: Skip or go light on feta if watching saturated fat closely.
Add roasted sweet potato for more substance.

name: Shrimp and Mango Salad
description: Grilled shrimp over greens with mango, red pepper, herbs, and a lime-fish sauce dressing.
why: A classic pick if shellfish isn't a concern for you, and the mango adds natural sweetness without added sugar.
mods: Ask for dressing on the side, lime and fish sauce dressings can be poured heavy.
watch: The lime-forward dressing is bright but acidic, worth noticing if reflux is a priority today.

name: Quinoa Tabbouleh with Chicken
description: Grilled chicken over quinoa tabbouleh with parsley, tomato, cucumber, and lemon.
why: Plant protein and fiber working together in the quinoa base, plus a real dose of vegetables.
mods: Extra parsley and cucumber add volume without adding much else.

name: Vietnamese Grilled Beef Salad
description: Grilled lemongrass beef over rice vermicelli noodles and greens, topped with peanuts, herbs, and nước chấm.
why: Choose a leaner cut and let the herbs and broth-style dressing carry the richness, this stays lighter than it tastes.
mods: Ask for nước chấm on the side so you're deciding how much goes on.
Extra herbs and greens in place of some noodles adds fiber.

name: Grilled Chicken and Avocado Wrap
description: Grilled chicken, avocado, lettuce, and tomato rolled in a whole wheat wrap.
why: A solid protein base, especially with extra vegetables piled on. Easy to take with you.
mods: Skip the mayo or ask for it on the side, avocado already brings the creaminess.

name: Tuna Salad Sandwich
description: Tuna salad on whole wheat bread with lettuce and tomato.
why: Lean and dense, almost no saturated fat in the tuna itself, the mayo is the one place worth going light.
mods: Ask for light mayo or half mayo, half Greek yogurt if you're making it at home.

name: Turkey and Hummus Wrap
description: Sliced turkey with hummus, spinach, and cucumber in a whole wheat wrap.
why: Lean and simple, a dependable everyday choice, and the hummus adds fiber the deli meat alone wouldn't.
mods: Pile on extra spinach and cucumber for more volume at no extra cost.
watch: Deli turkey can run higher in sodium than home-roasted, worth keeping in mind if it's a frequent lunch.

name: Egg Salad Sandwich
description: Egg salad on whole wheat bread with lettuce.
why: A reliable, familiar sandwich. Eggs bring genuine protein without needing much else.
mods: Mash in avocado instead of some of the mayo for a lighter version.

name: Falafel Wrap with Tahini
description: Falafel with lettuce, tomato, pickles, and tahini sauce in a warm pita.
why: Plant protein and fiber that doubles as the spread. A genuinely filling vegetarian option.
mods: Ask for tahini on the side, it's rich and easy to overpour.
A side salad instead of fries keeps this lighter.
watch: Falafel is typically fried, worth knowing going in even though the chickpea base is a plus.

name: Lentil and Vegetable Soup
description: A hearty lentil soup with carrot, celery, and tomato in a light vegetable broth.
why: One of the best soluble-fiber foods out there, often linked to healthier cholesterol numbers, and this soup leans on it heavily.
mods: Add a piece of crusty whole grain bread on the side if you want more staying power.

name: Chicken and Rice Soup
description: Shredded chicken and rice in a light broth with carrot, celery, and dill.
why: A familiar, easy protein to add to any broth. Gentle and warming when you want something simple.
mods: Add extra vegetables for more fiber and volume without more rice.

name: Miso Soup with Tofu and Seaweed
description: A light miso broth with soft tofu, wakame seaweed, and scallion.
why: Soaks up broth flavor while adding plant protein. About as gentle a starter or light meal as it gets.
mods: Pair with a rice bowl if you want this to be more of a full meal.
watch: Miso broth is concentrated in sodium even though the flavor reads as mild.

name: Butternut Squash Soup
description: Roasted butternut squash blended smooth with onion, garlic, and a touch of nutmeg.
why: Creamy texture without any actual cream if made with a light hand. A genuinely comforting, fiber-forward soup.
mods: Ask if it's made with cream, and if so, ask for a smaller portion or split it.
watch: Restaurant versions sometimes add cream for texture, worth asking about if cholesterol is top of mind.

name: Black Bean Soup
description: Black beans simmered with onion, garlic, and cumin, topped with a squeeze of lime and cilantro.
why: A clean, cholesterol-free protein option that's genuinely filling on its own, thanks to the fiber.
mods: Add a spoonful of Greek yogurt in place of sour cream for extra protein.

name: Pad Thai with Shrimp
description: Rice noodles stir-fried with shrimp, egg, bean sprouts, and a tamarind-fish sauce dressing, topped with peanuts and lime.
why: A classic pick if shellfish isn't a concern for you, and the tamarind sauce adds brightness without cream or heavy oil.
mods: Ask for less oil, pad thai can be made much lighter than the typical restaurant version.
Extra bean sprouts and vegetables add volume for the same noodle portion.
watch: Restaurant pad thai often runs sweeter and oilier than a home version.

name: Peanut Sesame Noodles with Chicken
description: Wheat noodles tossed in a peanut-sesame sauce with shredded chicken, cucumber, and carrot.
why: An easy way to add protein to almost any noodle bowl, and the vegetables add real crunch and volume.
mods: Ask for sauce on the side, peanut-based dressings are rich and easy to overpour.
watch: The peanut-sesame sauce is the richest part of this dish by a wide margin.

name: Garlic Noodles with Tofu
description: Egg noodles tossed in a garlicky butter-soy sauce with crispy tofu and scallion.
why: A plant-based option that holds up well in sauce, keeps the bowl from being carb-only.
mods: Ask for the sauce lighter, it's a butter-forward dish by design.
Add steamed broccoli or bok choy for fiber and volume.
watch: This dish is built around butter and garlic, it leans rich no matter how it's ordered.

name: Dan Dan Noodles
description: Wheat noodles in a spicy sesame-chili sauce with ground pork and preserved vegetables.
why: Keeps the bowl from being carb-only thanks to the ground pork, but this one runs genuinely spicy.
mods: Ask for less chili oil if you want to dial the heat down.
A side of steamed greens balances the richness of the sauce.
watch: This is one of the spicier options here, worth noticing if reflux is a priority today.

name: Soba Noodles with Edamame
description: Chilled soba noodles with edamame, cucumber, and a light sesame-soy dressing.
why: A plant-based option that holds up well cold, and buckwheat soba brings more fiber than a typical wheat noodle.
mods: Add grilled tofu or salmon if you want more protein.

name: Overnight Oats with Berries
description: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk with mixed berries, chia seeds, and a drizzle of honey.
why: A genuinely fiber-forward start to the day, and it's ready before you are since it's made the night before.
mods: Use oat or almond milk instead of whole milk if you're watching saturated fat.
Skip the honey, the berries bring plenty of natural sweetness.

name: Veggie Egg White Omelet
description: Egg whites folded around spinach, mushroom, and tomato, with a side of whole grain toast.
why: One of the more reliably cholesterol-friendly proteins around, plus a real dose of vegetables before noon.
mods: Add avocado on the toast for healthy fat and fiber together.

name: Greek Yogurt Parfait
description: Greek yogurt layered with granola and fresh berries.
why: Plain Greek yogurt is genuinely high in protein and low in the added sugar flavored versions carry.
mods: Choose plain yogurt and add your own honey to control the sugar.
Go light on granola, it's the most calorie-dense part of the bowl.
watch: Flavored yogurt and store-bought granola can both carry more added sugar than expected.

name: Avocado Toast with Egg
description: Mashed avocado on whole grain toast, topped with a fried or poached egg and chili flake.
why: A reliable, satisfying combination: healthy fat, fiber, and a real protein all in one plate.
mods: Add tomato or microgreens for more volume without much effort.

name: Congee with Ginger and Scallion
description: Slow-simmered rice porridge topped with ginger, scallion, and a soft egg.
why: About as gentle on the stomach as a meal gets, a good choice on a day when you want something easy to digest.
mods: Add shredded chicken or tofu for more protein.
watch: This is a lighter meal on its own, worth pairing with a protein if it's your main meal of the day.

name: Smoked Salmon Bagel
description: A toasted bagel with cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, and red onion.
why: Smoked salmon still brings real omega-3s, the cream cheese is the one place worth going lighter.
mods: Ask for light or half cream cheese, the salmon and capers carry plenty of flavor on their own.
A half bagel with extra salmon shifts the balance in a good direction.
watch: Smoked salmon and capers both bring real sodium, worth knowing if you're having this often.

name: Iced Oat Milk Matcha Latte
description: Whisked matcha over ice with oat milk and a light drizzle of honey.
why: A gentler caffeine curve than coffee for a lot of people, and oat milk keeps this easy on saturated fat.
mods: Ask for half the usual sweetener, most shops default to quite sweet.
Unsweetened with a splash of extra matcha adds flavor without adding sugar.

name: Unsweetened Matcha with Almond Milk
description: Whisked matcha with unsweetened almond milk, no added sweetener.
why: This is the one to feel best about for your teeth either way, genuinely low-sugar without losing the ritual.
mods: A splash of vanilla extract adds warmth without adding sugar.

name: Golden Turmeric Latte
description: Steamed milk whisked with turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, and a touch of honey.
why: A warming, caffeine-free ritual drink, a good option later in the day when you want something soothing.
mods: Oat or almond milk keeps this lighter than a whole milk version.

name: Ginger Lemon Tea
description: Fresh ginger and lemon steeped in hot water with a small amount of honey.
why: Genuinely soothing for digestion for a lot of people, and essentially calorie-free on its own.
mods: Skip the honey entirely if you want this completely unsweetened.
watch: The lemon makes this one to notice if citrus tends to trigger reflux for you.
